title: Feeding 6 Well Plates
author: Andrea Argouarch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8gihtue

steps.title: Record biopsy observations
steps.instruction: Observe each biopsy piece and note that it should appear dense and dark with clean, straight edges; morphology will not change. Expect outgrowth to appear anywhere from a few days up to 2 weeks depending on the biopsy.

steps.title: Turn off UV and clean hood
steps.instruction: Switch off the UV lights in the biosafety cabinet and wipe the interior surfaces with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare sterile complete media
steps.instruction: Wipe all items (pipettes, tubes, media bottles) with 70 % ethanol and bring them into the hood. Prepare complete DMEM high‑glucose, pyruvate media containing:

steps.title: Remove old media
steps.instruction: Using a vacuum line, carefully aspirate the old media from each well, taking care not to touch the coverslip.

steps.title: Add fresh media
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of the prepared complete media to each well slowly, ensuring the coverslip remains firmly and evenly positioned over the biopsy. Do not tilt the plate while adding media to prevent the coverslip from sliding.

substeps.instruction: Confirm coverslip is still firmly and evenly over the tissue

steps.title: Incubate plate
steps.instruction: Gently place the 6‑well plate into a humidified incubator set to 5 % CO₂ and 37 °C.

steps.title: Maintain feeding schedule
steps.instruction: After one week, gently change the media and thereafter feed the cultures every 2–3 days for up to 3 weeks to allow cells to emerge and expand from the tissue.

steps.title: Clean hood post‑procedure
steps.instruction: Wipe the biosafety cabinet interior with 70 % ethanol and turn the UV lights back on to sterilize the workspace.

description: Update cell culture notes in lab notebook
